title: Alice Babbs and the Second Sacred Concert
summary: Cootie praises Alice Babbs, for whom Duke wrote, as another Ellington voice.

venues.name: Cathedral of St. John the Divine

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: No. It's very remarkable. Well, Cootie, then 1968 was that second Sacred Concert at the Cathedral of St. John the Divine. I just wanted to talk to you about that beautiful voice, Alice Babbs. Surely you love that voice, don't you?
Yeah. Oh, she had a wonderful voice. A terrific voice.
Don't you think that what she had was something that absolutely belonged in there with the band? That sound. Or do you?
Yeah.
I don't want to put words in your mouth.
Well, no. That's what Duke -- Duke
wrote the thing for her.
Yeah.
He had her in mind, writing it.
Yeah. So, in other words, he did for her --
Yeah.
-- like he did for the guys in the band.
So she was another Ellington voice, really.
Yeah.
Yeah. Of course, he did that with Kay Davis, too, didn't he?
Yeah.
He wrote things for Kay Davis.
Uh-huh.
But I don't think there was ever a voice that he wrote anything for that could equal hers. Do you?
Who?
Alice Babs.
No.
No. I mean, you know, there have been other singers that have done the 'Sacred Concert' since, but it's not the same thing, really is it?
No.
